- **Polished the *Visa for a Hilsa* v2 script** against the comic playbook, as was done for *Snow*
  ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_sam-feedback-snow-hilsa.plan.md)). It has 7 boards, 36 panels and
  20–116 words a page.
  - Added an ASCII grid for each page, pinned looks for the cast and Shapla's three foremothers,
    the through-lines (the brass pot, the tag, two fixed camera positions on the hut) and the
    lettering rules.
  - Two new cast members to make before building: *the brass pot* and *Jalal and Shapla's hut*.
  - Fixed playbook breaks in the draft. The page 2 telemetry had been drawn into the art; it is
    now lettered labels. "Out of frame" and "glow" were in prompts.
  - Ya's tablet is now her e-paper notebook from *Snow*, and Taro appears on every page from 2 on.
  - Page 5's punchline is one large silent panel. On page 7, Ya leaving and Jalal's outburst
    share one panel, so the final boat gets half the board.
  - Edited Drafts now has a "Scene 0: Story of the Wife (TBW)" heading, which the prologue fills.
  - At Yan's request, wrote it into the *Script: Visa for a Hilsa* tab above Version 1, using
    `script-to-doc.py`. Nothing in the tab was changed.
- **Built *Visa for a Hilsa* on A1** (`VH`, `d89a6f17…`): 7 boards, 36 panels, each page
  lettered and checked in Chrome.
  - New cast: *the brass pot* and *Jalal and Shapla's hut*. Jalal (moustache, white vest) and
    Shapla (green sari, low bun) got pinned descriptions and new sheets. All four sheets were
    clean first time.
  - Redraws:
    - 1.8: two fish instead of one.
    - 2.2: a blank teal band and garbled drawn words. 2.3 and 2.5: brown hilsa instead of silver.
    - 3.4 and 3.6: no room for lettering. 3.6 again: Ya's hologram came out in full colour, fixed
      by leaving her out of `cast`.
    - 4.4: blank. 4.5: drawn notebook label, sub-panels, faces at the top, then green walls.
    - 5.1: strangers instead of Jalal and Shapla. 5.3: green walls. 5.4: Ya drawn as a man, and a
      drawn strip.
    - 6.3: green walls. 7.4: the boat's direction (three tries).
  - Open for Yan: in 7.4 the boat still heads left, towards the village Shapla looks back at.
  - Five new rows in the playbook's table of fixes; canon production state updated.
- **Khai's notes on *Hilsa*, folded into the script** (local draft; not yet in the doc or the
  comic). It is now 8 boards and 41 panels.
  - A new page 2, set in 2048: Shapla's mother turns down PREMISE's funds, because of the last
    mile and generations of distrust. Shapla (15) meets Jalal (17), and mercury from the river's
    fish is planted.
  - Page 8, in Yan's shape: Ya stays the night, wakes to the couple arguing, and cooks breakfast
    with Shapla. Shapla accepts Jalal joining KAN's data collection. Ya explains that following
    the fish means a varied diet, the answer to the mercury.
  - Yan kept the dates: 2048, not Khai's 2030s, which the birth years rule out.
  - New cast cards: Shapla at 8 (sheet redrawn to drop a drawn border), Shapla at 15, Jalal at 17,
    Shapla's mother.
- **Rebuilt *Hilsa* to the revised script.** VH is now 8 boards and 41 panels; the script tab's v2
  section was replaced after checking it was unchanged.
  - Page 1's bottom half became one large panel: the arrival on the Meghna.
  - New page 2. Page 8 was split into five panels and redrawn.
  - Pages 3–7 kept their art; the rest was renumbered.
  - Redraws:
    - 8.4: blank at first. A later take had both tails meeting at Ya, so it was redrawn with Ya on
      the left and Shapla on the right, and without the bindi Shapla had acquired. Shapla's cast
      description now says no bindi.
    - 8.5: the drone came out as an aeroplane. The new take finally sails right, away from the
      village.
  - Khai, via Yan: they are not poor in the Pluriverse. Two lines changed: 7.3 back to
    "Wherever the fish go…", and 8.1 "That was our chance to follow the hilsa!". The better diet
    is now the reason to move.
- **Page 1 captions in Yan's words:** one woman's line, generation by generation. 1947, her
  life cut in two; 1971, her daughter runs; the 2040s, her great-granddaughter leaves the delta;
  then "This is the story of Shapla." The pot is no longer named in the lettering (Yan).

    typos in 2.4: "its problems" and "runs deep".
- **A ninth page for the ending** (Yan): VH is now 9 boards and 46 panels.
  - 8.4: Shapla describes the numbness. The new image is panned up for headroom rather than
    redrawn.
  - 8.5: an atlas panorama of the foods along the hilsa's route, with Ya's explanation and a
    caption on clearing the mercury. The caption covers a stray crab badge the model drew.
  - Page 9: Shapla takes the pot down, Jalal learns the data work, Shapla packs food, the goodbye

    "worthless" (4.3).
  - Synced the script and the doc tab with the live comic. A small script carried each live

- **Consistency audit of VH.** Viewed every page's images full size in a grid, plus Yan's catches
  (8.1, 4.3, 6.4).
  - Ya's hair tied back (7.1, 8.1): her cast description now says the bob is ALWAYS loose, with a
    fringe, never tied back.
  - The river drawn as sand (4.3): teal again.
  - 6.4: the bindi was back, Jalal was heavier and cartoonish, and the curry dish was huge. Now he
    is wiry, the plate dinner-sized and the gamcha plain.
  - 7.1: two pots, Ya's hair tied back; its first redraw also brought back green walls and the
    bindi. All fixed.
  - 9.4: a plain sail, unlike the boat's patched teal-and-brown one.
  - **The bindi recurs** even with "no bindi" in Shapla's cast description; only putting it first in
    the prompt, as "Important: …", held. The playbook notes the same for wall colour.
- **Sam on 8.5:** "balanced diet vs. mercury poisoning" is not sound medical advice for the spine of
  a happy story. Ya now calls a KAN doctor (Yan's lettering), and the bottom panel is split in two:
  - 8.5, a KAN permaculture garden for a varied diet;
  - 8.6, a KAN barefoot doctor.

  My caption claiming that "the mercury leaves the body" is deleted; Sam is writing the new one.
  - The first doctor came out as a white man. Yan: it should be someone from a neighbouring
    village, so the doctor is now a village woman in a faded sari and the KAN waistcoat.
  - 8.4 still had Shapla's bindi, which my audit missed; it is now redrawn.
- **Swapped 8.5 and 8.6** (Yan): the doctor first, then the garden. Images and balloons moved
  together, and the gardener's tail was re-aimed.
- **4K print versions of all 47 VH panels** (about $7). 4.4 failed to store once; the retry worked.
  - Pages 1–4 compared with their drafts: faithful. One small drift: 4.3's sail gained red patches.
  - Pages 5–9 left for Yan's manual check, at Yan's request.
- **Redrew the Sunda maps (PAO:3:1, 3:2) from real geodata**
  ([plan](../plans/2026-10-03_sunda-geodata-maps.plan.md)). `scripts/sunda-maps.py` takes ETOPO
  2022, contours the −120 m lowstand coast, and routes flow over the exposed shelf. The drowned
  rivers come out of the data rather than being traced from the copyrighted moodboard maps.
  - It reproduced the reconstructions: a Gulf of Thailand paleo-lake, the Siam river joining the
    North Sunda trunk, and a mouth about 60 km from the flotel's 5°N 110°E.
  - Both maps are in the panels via `draw_panel_svg`, with labels as size-11 caption balloons.
  - Still open: "Pangaea's largest" in caption 3:2 is wrong by about 200 million years, and that
    caption runs under the top of its panel.
  - Started a Homebrew reinstall of GDAL (the old 3.3.2 had lost its poppler library), at Yan's
    request. ~~Homebrew~~ It failed: Homebrew no longer ships Intel-Mac bottles, and the source
    build died. Resolved with conda-forge instead: GDAL 3.13.3 (plus the netCDF, HDF5 and PDF
    drivers) in a micromamba env at `~/micromamba/envs/gdal`. The tools are symlinked into
    `~/.local/bin`, which comes before the still-broken brew 3.3.2 on PATH.
- **Pennant captions** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-03_pointed-captions.plan.md)). A caption can now
  have a pointed end (`point: left | right`) and a tilt (`rotation`, until now sfx-only), set from
  the inspector or the MCP. Lettering stays out of the art, so Sam's text stays editable.
  Deployed to production. The two PAO:4:2 captions are now tilted pennants, as in Sam's
  inspiration image.
  - The e2e test is written but has not run (it needs local Supabase, and Docker was down).
- **PAO:3:4** redrawn: everyday clothes (some everyday traditional wear, no costumes), a crowd
  that reflects the world's population, and Isma (18) and Dew (63) at the centre.
  **PAO:4:5**: the PESA agent is now Black. **PAO:3:2**: a bolder Sunda Summit marker.
- **PAO page 6: a second version of page 5**, recreating Sam's "The Pluriverse in Microcosm"
  infographic (slide `h131ac5edd0a73ed9_0_53`). The art is a glass-sphere watershed on the
  waterline, chained to the seabed. Sam's slide text is lettered on top: principles as cream
  circles, institutions as teal circles, systems as ochre boxes, and the purpose on a pennant.
  Page 5 is unchanged, so Yan can pick one.
  - Slide text slip: PROSPER's box repeats PESA's subtitle and description, so page 6 uses page 5's
    PROSPER text. PESA is "denizen-support" on the slide but "customer-support" on page 5.
- **PAO:2:6** redrawn so Isma and Dew are small in the crowd: at that size they were being read as
  the banker and the Summit speaker.
- **PAO:6:1** redrawn with the composition moved up: smaller sphere, short chain, and the anchor rock on
  the seabed visible between the bottom boxes.
- **Prologue and Act One: proofread and print versions.** Fixed REPRESENTATIVE→S (3:4),
  SPECIALLY DESIGNED (3:3), dashes, a stray "..." and double spaces (2:6, 2:3, 4:2, 4:5). Per Yan,
  also changed CONVENED TO→AT and ENTRUSTED INTO→TO PLURIVERS (4:2 and PROSPER on pages 4 and 5).
  Left as written at Yan's call: "all walks of the world", "domino-ing", the doubled Great
  Pluriversalization heading, PROSPER's "them". Pangaea had already been fixed to "Earth's".
  Made 4K print versions of all 21 image panels (about $3; the two vector maps need none). Added the
  page 1 title "PROLOGUE: SIX DISASTERS, ONE DREAM", styled like page 5's.
- **4K print versions went wrong on three panels, now fixed** (80bb4e4, deployed). The print
  prompt's "do not add any text" made the model erase PAO:1:7's "DRAFT US A PLAN". Naming the
  palette as where the colours "come from" let it recolour 1:4 (brown floodwater turned teal, with
  a seam) and 1:6 (smoke turned white). Yan caught 1:7.
  - Compared every 4K take side by side with its source in the browser.
  - New prompt (`print-prompt.ts`): keep existing lettering letter for letter, no recolouring, the
    palette only as a hue reference. Redid 1:4 and 1:7, which now match. 1:6 needed a second go:
    it matches except two cloud gaps turned cream.
  - Lesson: a print version is a redraw, not an upscale. Compare every one before it goes to print.
